answer: The admission bond is time locked for 13 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Locks are recorded in comet, expire in pigment, and plume lists each expiry. An adversary running 150 aliases thus needs 179 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. A farm of 589 identities would post 4664 proofs and burn roughly 51 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
